facts.statement: Ornithomimus lived during the Campanian to Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: fossil_range: Late Cretaceous (Campanian to Maastrichtian),

facts.statement: Ornithomimus was a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaurs found in western North America during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Ornithomimus (; "bird mimic") is a genus of ornithomimid theropod dinosaurs from the Campanian and Maastrichtian ages of the Late Cretaceous in western North America.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus was a swift, bipedal dinosaur covered in feathers with a small toothless beak, suggesting an omnivorous diet.
facts.quote: Ornithomimus was a swift, bipedal dinosaur which was covered in feathers and equipped with a small toothless beak that may indicate an omnivorous diet.

facts.statement: The type species Ornithomimus velox was named in 1890 by Othniel Charles Marsh based on fossils from the Denver Formation of Colorado.
facts.quote: O. velox was named in 1890 by Othniel Charles Marsh on the basis of a foot and partial hand from the Denver Formation of Colorado.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus velox was named in 1890 by O.C. Marsh based on a partial hindlimb and forelimb found by George Lyman Cannon on June 30, 1889.
facts.quote: The type species, Ornithomimus velox, was first named by O.C. Marsh in 1890 and is based on syntypes YPM 542 and YPM 548 (a partial hindlimb and forelimb, respectively), found by George Lyman Cannon in the Denver Formation of Colorado on June 30, 1889.

facts.statement: The name Ornithomimus means "bird mimic" and refers to the dinosaur's bird-like foot.
facts.quote: The generic name means "bird mimic", derived from Greek words ὄρνις (ornis), "bird", and μῖμος (mimos), "mimic", in reference to the bird-like foot.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus edmontonicus was named in 1933 by Charles Mortram Sternberg based on a nearly complete skeleton from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation.
facts.quote: Also in 1933, Charles Mortram Sternberg named the species Ornithomimus edmontonicus for a nearly complete skeleton from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation (specimen CMN 8632).

facts.statement: Ornithomimus is usually classified into two species: Ornithomimus velox and Ornithomimus edmontonicus.
facts.quote: It is usually classified into two species: the type species, Ornithomimus velox, and a referred species, Ornithomimus edmontonicus.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Coelosaurus antiquus belongs to Ornithomimus, with some researchers considering it a nomen dubium.
facts.quote: However, David Weishampel (2004) considered "C." antiquus to be indeterminate among ornithomimosaurs, resulting in it being a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul classified several genera including Archaeornithomimus, Struthiomimus, Dromiceiomimus, and Gallimimus as species of Ornithomimus in 1988, though this view is not widely accepted.
facts.quote: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul classified the various species of Archaeornithomimus, Struthiomimus, Dromiceiomimus, and Gallimimus to the genus Ornithomimus.

facts.statement: The first Ornithomimus fossil was found in 1889 and described by American paleontologist Othniel C. Marsh in 1890.
facts.quote: El primer fósil de Ornithomimus fue encontrado en 1889 y descrito por el paleontólogo estadounidense Othniel C. Marsh en 1890.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus lived during the late Cretaceous, approximately 70 to 66 million years ago in the Maastrichtian stage, in what is now North America.
facts.quote: Ornithomimus (lat. "imitador de las aves") es un género conocido por dos especies de dinosaurios terópodos ornitomímidos que vivieron a finales del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 70 a 66 millones de años, en el Maastrichtiense, en lo que hoy es Norteamérica.

facts.statement: The type species of Ornithomimus is Ornithomimus velox.
facts.quote: type_species: Ornithomimus velox

facts.statement: Ornithomimus edmontonicus, described by Sternberg in 1933, is recognized as a subdivision of the genus.
facts.quote: subdivision: Ornithomimus edmontonicus Sternberg, 1933

facts.statement: Ornithomimus was bipedal and superficially resembled ratites.
facts.quote: They were bipedal and superficially resemblant to ratites.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus would have been swift runners due to its very long limbs and hollow bones.
facts.quote: They would have been swift runners thanks to their very long limbs and hollow bones.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus had large brains and large eyes.
facts.quote: They also had large brains and large eyes.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of Ornithomimus edmontonicus at 3.8 meters and its weight at 170 kilograms.
facts.quote: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated the length of O. edmontonicus at 3.8 m and its weight at 170 kg.

facts.statement: A fourth feathered Ornithomimus specimen, described in October 2015 by Aaron van der Reest, Alex Wolfe, and Phil Currie, was the first to preserve tail feathers.
facts.quote: A fourth feathered specimen of Ornithomimus, this time from the lower portion of the Dinosaur Park Formation, was described in October of 2015 by Aaron van der Reest, Alex Wolfe, and Phil Currie. It was the first Ornithomimus specimen to preserve the feathers of its tail.

facts.statement: The diet of Ornithomimus is debated; while theropods might have been carnivorous, its body shape suggests a largely omnivorous lifestyle.
facts.quote: The diet of Ornithomimus is still highly debated. As theropods, ornithomimids might have been carnivorous, but their body shape would have been suited for a largely omnivorous lifestyle.

facts.statement: Large eye sockets suggest Ornithomimus had a keen visual sense and possibly lived nocturnally.
facts.quote: The large eye sockets suggest a keen visual sense and also suggest the possibility that they were nocturnal.

facts.statement: A 2001 study by Bruce Rothschild and others examined 178 Ornithomimus foot bones for stress fractures but found none.
facts.quote: In a 2001 study conducted by Bruce Rothschild and other paleontologists, 178 foot bones referred to Ornithomimus were examined for signs of stress fracture, but none were found.

facts.statement: A 2010 re-evaluation by Lindsay Zanno and colleagues cast doubt on the assignment of a Kaiparowits Formation specimen to O. velox and possibly even to Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: Re-evaluation of this specimen by Lindsay Zanno and colleagues in 2010, however, cast doubt on its assignment to O. velox and possibly even to Ornithomimus.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus species had small skulls and light bones, suggesting they were agile and capable of high speeds.
facts.quote: Todas las especies de ornitomímidos poseían un pequeño cráneo y huesos ligeros, lo cual sugiere que eran ágiles y alcanzaban altas velocidades.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus species had three-toed feet, long thin arms, long necks, and bird-like toothless skulls with beaks.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros ornitomímidos, las especies de Ornithomimus se caracterizan por pies con tres dedos que soportan peso, brazos largos y delgados y cuellos largos con cráneos con forma de pájaro, alargados, sin dientes y con pico.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus was bipedal, superficially resembled an ostrich, and was likely a fast runner.
facts.quote: Eran bípedos y superficialmente se parecían a un avestruz. Hubieran sido corredores rápidos.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus had very long limbs, hollow bones, and large brains and eyes.
facts.quote: Tenían extremidades muy largas, huesos huecos y grandes cerebros y ojos.

facts.statement: While ornithomimid brains were large for non-avian dinosaurs, some paleontologists suggest the enlargement was for kinesthetic coordination rather than higher intelligence.
facts.quote: Los cerebros de los ornitomímidos en general eran grandes para los dinosaurios no aviares, pero esto puede no ser necesariamente un signo de mayor inteligencia; Algunos paleontólogos piensan que las porciones agrandadas del cerebro estaban dedicadas a la coordinación cinestésica.

facts.statement: Henry Fairfield Osborn suggested that Ornithomimus hand bones, which resemble sloth bones, were used to hook branches while feeding.
facts.quote: Los huesos de las manos son notablemente parecidos al de los perezosos en apariencia, lo que llevó Henry Fairfield Osborn sugiere que fueron utilizados para enganchar ramas durante la alimentación.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus differed from other ornithomimids like Struthiomimus by having shorter torsos, long thin forearms, very thin straight claws on hands and feet, and similar lengths for hand bones, metacarpals, and fingers.
facts.quote: Ornithomimus difiere de otros ornitomímidos, como Struthiomimus, en tener torsos más cortos, antebrazos largos y delgados, garras muy delgadas, rectas de manos y pies y tener los huesos de las manos, metacarpianos, y dedos de longitudes similares.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus was likely omnivorous, eating leaves, fruits, small mammals, reptiles, shellfish, insects, and eggs due to its toothless beak.
facts.quote: Su pico sin dientes les permitía comer diversos tipos de alimentos, con lo que probablemente eran omnívoro, alimentándose de hojas, frutos, mamíferos y reptiles pequeños, mariscos, insectos e incluso huevos.

facts.statement: In 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimated O. edmontonicus to be 3.8 meters long and weigh 170 kilograms.
facts.quote: En 2010, Gregory S. Paul estimó la longitud de O. edmontonicus en 3,8 metros, su peso en 170 kilogramos.

facts.statement: Specimen CMN 12228 preserves a femur measuring 46.8 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: Una de sus muestras, CMN 12228, conserva un fémur, hueso del muslo, de 46,8 centímetros de largo.

facts.statement: Starting in 1995, several Ornithomimus specimens preserving feather evidence have been found.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, a partir de 1995, se han encontrado varios especímenes de Ornithomimus que conservan evidencia de plumas.

facts.statement: A 2012 study concluded O. edmontonicus was covered in downy feathers at all growth stages, with only adults having moderate bird-like wing structures, suggesting wings evolved for mating displays.
facts.quote: Un estudio que describió los fósiles en 2012 concluyó que O. edmontonicus estaba cubierto de plumas plumosas en todas las etapas de crecimiento, y que solo los adultos tenían estructuras parecidas a alas de aves moderans, lo que sugiere que las alas pueden haber evolucionado para exhibiciones de apareamiento.

facts.statement: In 2014, Christian Foth and others argued evidence was insufficient to conclude Ornithomimus forelimb feathers were necessarily pennaceous, noting monofilamentous cassowary wing feathers might leave similar traces.
facts.quote: En 2014, Christian Foth y otros argumentaron que la evidencia era insuficiente para concluir que las plumas de las extremidades anteriores de Ornithomimus eran necesariamente pennáceas, citando el hecho de que las plumas de ala monofilamentosas en casuarios probablemente dejarían rastros similares.

facts.statement: In October 2015, Aaron van der Reest, Alex Wolfe, and Phil Currie described a fourth feathered Ornithomimus specimen from the lower Dinosaur Park Formation.
facts.quote: Aaron van der Reest, Alex Wolfe y Phil Currie describieron en octubre de 2015 un cuarto espécimen emplumado de Ornithomimus, esta vez de la parte inferior de la Formación Dinosaur Park.

facts.statement: Skin impressions from the 2015 specimen showed bare skin from mid-thigh to feet and a skin flap connecting the upper thigh to the torso.
facts.quote: Las impresiones de la piel también se conservaron en la muestra de 2015, que indicaba que desde la mitad del muslo hasta los pies, había piel desnuda sin escamas, y que un colgajo de piel conectaba la parte superior del muslo al torso.

facts.statement: The generic name means "bird imitator," derived from Greek ornis (bird) and mimos (imitator), referring to the bird-like foot.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico significa "imitador de pájaro", derivado del griego ὄρνις, ornis, "pájaro" y μῖμος, mimos, "imitador", en referencia al pie de ave.

facts.statement: The specific name means "swift" in Latin.
facts.quote: El nombre específico significa "veloz" en latín.

facts.statement: O. altus was named in 1902 by Lawrence Lambe based on hindlimbs found in Alberta in 1901, but was renamed to the separate genus Struthiomimus in 1916 by Henry Fairfield Osborn.
facts.quote: Una sexta especie, Ornithomimus altus, fue nombrada en 1902 por Lawrence Lambe, basada en el espécimen CMN 930, extremidades posteriores encontradas en 1901 en Alberta, pero este fue en 1916 renombrado a un género separado, Struthiomimus, por Henry Fairfield Osborn.

facts.statement: In 1933, Charles Mortram Sternberg named O. edmontonicus based on an almost complete skeleton from the Horseshoe Canyon Formation of Alberta, specimen CMN 8632.
facts.quote: En 1933, Charles Mortram Sternberg nombró a la especie Ornithomimus edmontonicus como un esqueleto casi completo de la Formación cañón herradura de Alberta , el espécimen CMN 8632.

facts.statement: Marsh initially thought Ornithomimus was an ornithopod, but this changed after Hatcher found a partial ornithomimid skeleton in Wyoming, which Marsh named O. sedens in 1892.
facts.quote: Al principio, Marsh asumió que Ornithomimus era un ornitópodo, pero esto cambió cuando Hatcher encontró el espécimen USNM 4736, un esqueleto de un ornitomímido parcial, en Wyoming, que Marsh llamó Ornithomimus sedens en 1892.

facts.statement: In 1920, Charles Whitney Gilmore named O. affinis for Dryosaurus grandis based on indeterminate material, a classification that is now considered dubious.
facts.quote: En 1920 Charles Whitney Gilmore nombró Ornithomimus affinis para Dryosaurus grandis de Lull 1911, basado en material indeterminado.

facts.statement: In 1933, William Arthur Parks created O. elegans, which is now seen as belonging to Chirostenotes or Elmisaurus.
facts.quote: En 1933, William Arthur Parks creó un Ornithomimus elegans, visto hoy como perteneciente a Chirostenotes o Elmisaurus.

facts.statement: In 1972, Dale Russell published a morphometric study showing that statistical differences in proportions could distinguish Ornithomimus from Struthiomimus.
facts.quote: En 1972 Dale Russell publicó un estudio morfométrico que muestra que las diferencias estadísticas en algunas proporciones podrían usarse para distinguir los dos.

facts.statement: Joseph Leidy named two tibiae from the Navesink Formation of New Jersey Coelosaurus antiquus in 1865.
facts.quote: Dos tibias de la Formación Navesink de Nueva Jersey fueron nombradas Coelosaurus antiquus, "lagarto hueco antiguo", por Joseph Leidy en 1865.

facts.statement: Donald Baird and John R. Horner first attributed the tibiae to Ornithomimus in 1979 as O. antiquus.
facts.quote: Las tibias fueron atribuidas por primera vez a Ornithomimus en 1979 por Donald Baird y John R. Horner como Ornithomimus antiquus.

facts.statement: In 2004, David Weishampel considered Coelosaurus antiquus an indeterminate and therefore dubious ornithomimosaur.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, David Weishampel en 2004, consideró "C". antiquus como un ornitomimosaurio indeterminado y por lo tanto dudoso.

facts.statement: In 1988, Gregory S. Paul classified species from Archaeornithomimus, Struthiomimus, Dromiceiomimus, and Gallimimus into the genus Ornithomimus.
facts.quote: En 1988 Gregory S. Paul clasificó las especies de los géneros Archaeornithomimus , Struthiomimus , Dromiceiomimus y Gallimimus en el género Ornithomimus.

facts.statement: In 1890, Othniel Charles Marsh assigned Ornithomimus to the family Ornithomimosauria.
facts.quote: En 1890, Marsh asignó Ornithomimus a Ornithomimosauria , una clasificación que todavía es común.

facts.statement: Modern cladistic studies indicate a derived position within Ornithomimidae, but they have only included O. edmontonicus in their analyses.
facts.quote: Los estudios cladísticos modernos indican una posición derivada en las ornitomímidos, estos, sin embargo, solo han incluido O. edmontonicus en sus análisis.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian stages, between 83.6 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: The diet of Ornithomimus is debated; while they might have been carnivores like most theropods, their body shape also suggests a partially or largely herbivorous lifestyle.
facts.quote: La dieta de Ornithomimus todavía se debate. Como la mayoría de los terópodos, las ornitomímidos podrían haber sido carnívoros, pero su forma corporal también habría sido adecuada para un estilo de vida en parte o en gran parte herbívoro.

facts.statement: Suggested food items for Ornithomimus include insects, crustaceans, fruits, leaves, branches, eggs, and the flesh of lizards and small mammals.
facts.quote: La comida sugerida incluye insectos, crustáceos, frutas, hojas, ramas, huevos y la carne de lagartos y pequeños mamíferos.

facts.statement: Ornithomimus had legs clearly suited for rapid locomotion, with the tibia approximately 20% longer than the femur.
facts.quote: Ornithomimus tenía piernas que parecían claramente adecuadas para una locomoción rápida, con la tibia aproximadamente un 20% más larga que el fémur.

facts.statement: Large eye sockets suggest acute vision and the possibility that Ornithomimus was nocturnal.
facts.quote: Las cuencas de los ojos grandes sugieren un sentido visual agudo, y también sugieren la posibilidad de que fueran nocturnas.

facts.statement: In a 2001 study, Bruce Rothschild and colleagues examined 178 foot bones referred to Ornithomimus for stress fractures but found none.
facts.quote: En un estudio realizado en 2001 por Bruce Rothschild y otros paleontólogos, se examinaron 178 huesos del pie referidos a Ornithomimus para detectar signos de fractura por estrés, pero no se encontraron ninguno.

rejected.quote: In the latter, Russell recognised two species: the type species Ornithomimus velox and Ornithomimus edmontonicus (even though he had trouble reliably distinguishing it from O. velox).
